southeast IL which resides in a relatively stationary frontal zone. 
With a complex of strong thunderstorms that pushed eastward along 
roughly the I-74 corridor this morning, an outflow pushed southward 
across much of the area with cooler air and cloud cover tempering 
instability across much of the area. However, SPC mesoanalysis 
indicates strong MLCAPE around 4000 J/KG lingering south of I-70.

western portions of I-72 is showing effective bulk shear of 40-50 
kts and could drive another complex of severe storms as moves over 
that area this evening. SPC maintains a Slight Risk for severe 
storms in east-central and southeast IL, with damaging wind as the 
highest probability for severe weather (15% risk), but also a 2% 
tornado risk and 5% hail risk.

despite a few storms developing over the stalled frontal boundary, 
however another nocturnal MCS looks to be moving across IA 
overnight, heading toward northern or central IL Thursday morning.

deep layer bulk shear and 100-200 SRH, and additional severe storms 
will be possible, for which SPC depicts a Marginal Risk. The pattern 
will continue through Friday if not Saturday as well.

On Sunday, a cold front will traverse the area driven by a more 
potent shortwave moving through the northern states. Additional 
showers and thunderstorms may accompany this frontal passage, then a 
quieter period should ensue for early next week.

70s, yielding afternoon heat index values approaching 105 daily for 
portions of central and southeast IL, especially southern portions.
